subject: Availability tolerance & mitigation endorsement - Oceana HealthTech deal
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@oceanahealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.example
Cc: procurements@oceanahealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot production SLO tolerances (ask + timeline)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our infra and product teams scoped the initial pilot and we have two asks that will determine whether we can proceed to a production ramp:

1) Temporary uptime tolerance: for the first 90 days post-cutover we need a contractual tolerance of 99.2% regional availability (US) due to large warm-up traffic and customer onboarding spikes.
2) Latency guard: 95th percentile latency at or below 600ms for our typical 4k-token prompts; if we can't meet that we need a credit mechanism that scales with observed tail latency.

We understand these are outside Redwood's standard SLOs. In exchange we are prepared to sign a 12-month committed usage agreement (baseline commit = $420k ARR) and request a commercial concession (we're budgeting a 20% effective discount on hosted rates for the first six months while we stabilize).

Attached is our infra summary and a short risk note. Can your team propose an operational mitigation plan and an internal approval path? We need an answer by Friday, May 21 to keep the launch timeline.

Best,
Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Product, Oceana HealthTech
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.example
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@oceanahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot production SLO tolerances (ask + timeline)

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear ask and the materials. We can support a temporary deviation from our standard SLA for pilots, but we'll need an internal commercial and risk approval for the specific tolerance levels and the requested discount.

High-level proposal from product/ops to address your ask:
- Operational mitigation: staged cutover with a 2-week canary (10% traffic), region-by-region ramp, mandatory prefix/KV caching enabled, and an auto-fallback to a slightly smaller model variant if latency breaches threshold.
- Monitoring & guardrails: daily telemetry dashboard and weekly review cadence with your SREs for the first 60 days.
- Commercial trade: 6 months of a temporary effective price concession in exchange for a 12-month commit.

Internal ask: I need Deal Desk + VP Sales sign-off on the commercial concession and a limited SLO waiver (99.2% uptime for 90 days) with a defined credit cap. Can I loop in Marissa (Pricing) and Ben (Customer Ops) to help scope the credit exposure?

I'll attach an SLO impact model and a term sheet for internal review.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.example
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot production SLO tolerances (ask + timeline)

Sofia / Marissa — reviewed Asha's ask and the attached SLO_impact_model. Quick notes:

1) Credit sizing: we should cap aggregate monthly service credits for this pilot at 1.5% of the monthly invoice (not the 5% typical for larger concessions). Anything higher materially increases our risk profile for multi-tenant hosted capacity.
2) Discount: 20% for six months is a heavy concession versus our baseline. If we approve SLO leniency we'll need to trade for tougher operational levers: mandatory dedicated pool reservation after month 3 or an increased usage commit.
3) Fallbacks: require a hard-stop auto-fallback to the lower-latency model variant (documented in SOW) and a rollback to private/dedicated if incidents exceed agreed thresholds.

From ops perspective I'm comfortable with 99.2% for a limited window provided the fallout credit cap is 1.5% and the canary/rollback plan is codified.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot production SLO tolerances (ask + timeline)

Team — ran a quick cost / exposure model. Two alternative commercial structures we could present:

A) Concession = 20% for 6 months; Credit cap = 1.5% monthly invoice; Staged rollout with 2-week canary + mandatory dedicated pool option after month 3; Legal to add explicit failure modes that trigger migration to dedicated and termination rights after repeated incidents.

B) Concession = 15% for 6 months; SLO slightly tighter (99.4% uptime temporary); Credit cap = 1.0% monthly; Full canary + contingency plan as above.

Option B reduces our risk and still meets Oceana's timeline in most scenarios. If we go with A, we should require an exec-level authorization for the larger commercial concession.

Please advise which option we should present to the customer. If leadership signs off on A we should include a single-quarter escrowed credit reserve and explicit rollback triggers.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Product & Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.example
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, jonas_weber@redwood.example
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@oceanahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting executive authorization for commercial exception (Oceana HealthTech) — decision needed by 2027-05-21

Laura — we need an exec decision to finalize terms with Oceana by next Friday. Summary and recommended terms below (attached: DealTerm_Summary.docx & SOW_term_sheet_stub.pdf):

Customer: Oceana HealthTech (Pilot -> Prod ramp)
Ask: Temporary deviation from standard availability SLO: 99.2% regional uptime for 90 days + latency tolerance (95th <= 600ms)
Proposed commercial trade (recommended by Deal Desk): Option B (preferred):
- 15% effective discount for 6 months (applied to hosted usage)
- Credit cap: 1.0% of monthly billed amount for pilot window
- Operational controls: 2-week canary, autoscaling + KV caching, auto-fallback to model variant, weekly telemetry reviews with customer SREs
- Contingency: mandatory dedicated pool if incidents exceed thresholds for two consecutive weeks

Why this is safe: Option B reduces financial exposure, keeps clear rollback triggers, and is likely acceptable to Oceana given our operational mitigations. If leadership prefers to accept a 20% concession, that requires an explicit VP/Exec sign-off and an escrowed reserve to cover potential credits.

Requested action: please approve Option B (15% / 1.0% credit cap) or explicitly authorize Option A with the additional controls by EOD 2027-05-19 so we can present terms to customer and finalize SOW.

Thanks — I can hop on a 20-min sync if you'd prefer to talk through tradeoffs.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, jonas_weber@redwood.example
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@oceanahealth.com>, legal@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Requesting executive authorization for commercial exception (Oceana HealthTech) — decision needed by 2027-05-21

Team — thanks for the clear framing. I approve Option B with one modification: increase the credit cap to 1.5% of monthly billed amount (conservative cushion) while keeping the concession at 15% for six months. Conditions for approval:

1) Add explicit rollback and canary triggers in the SOW (documented thresholds & automated model fallback).
2) Legal to include a 90-day review clause and a requirement for weekly operational check-ins with Oceana SREs.
3) Finance to place a notch on the account to reserve for potential credits (informal reserve; not an escrow).

Sofia — you have my sign-off to present these revised terms to Oceana. Ben / Legal: please prepare the SOW addendum and the short-term credit schedule. Marissa: update pricing docs and confirm final margin impact.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
